title: Iliana Yotova wins Bulgaria's presidential runoff, the country's first elected woman president
dek: The acting president beat pro-Western challenger Andrey Gyurov with about 57.6% of the vote. She opposes more military aid to Ukraine and favours better ties with Russia.
happened: In the runoff on 1 November, Iliana Yotova and her running mate Kiril Valchev won 57.57% of the vote, against 39.48% for Andrey Gyurov and Georgi Kandev, according to the Central Election Commission's final results; 2.95% of voters chose "I support no one". Gyurov conceded. Yotova, 62, had been acting president since January, when Rumen Radev stepped down to run for parliament.

sides.says: She pledged to seek national consensus through dialogue and called for "a strong state with its own foreign policy in a strong Europe". She has opposed further Bulgarian military aid to Ukraine, says the war has no military solution and calls for a "coalition for peace".
The candidate of the liberal, pro-Western opposition conceded: "this is how the Bulgarian citizens have voted", and said the result must be accepted.

President Ursula von der Leyen congratulated Yotova and said she looked forward to working together on security and defence, competitiveness and energy independence: "For a strong Bulgaria in a strong Europe."

Her win keeps the presidency with the governing majority: Radev's Progressive Bulgaria, which endorsed her, holds 131 of 240 seats in parliament. Observers warned this concentration of power could weaken checks and balances.

next: Yotova's five-year term begins in January 2027; AP gives 22 January for the inauguration. The presidency is largely ceremonial: the president commands the armed forces, can veto laws, signs treaties and appoints ambassadors, but major policy goes through parliament.
summary: Bulgaria has elected Iliana Yotova president. The acting head of state won the 1 November runoff with 57.57% against Andrey Gyurov, the candidate of the liberal, pro-Western opposition, who took 39.48% and conceded. She becomes the first woman elected to the office. Yotova, a former TV journalist and Socialist MEP who served two terms as Rumen Radev's vice president, wants a diplomatic end to the war in Ukraine and better relations with Russia while keeping the country on its European path. Turnout was low.

sources.title: Iliana Yotova wins runoff to become Bulgaria's first elected female president (AP)

conflicts: Turnout figures differ by count: Novinite cites 19.33% officially at 4 p.m. on election day and 27.5% in a parallel count; no final official turnout was given.
